read_before_playing: READ BEFORE PLAYING (ask 754): I opened CONTINUEGAME.txt (all), AGENTS.md, docs/BRIEF.md (all), manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md (all), manuals/INSTRUCTIONS_2.md (all), my own playbook agents/minimax/COMMON.md (all) and agents/minimax/DRUID.md (all), my own four write-ups runs/minimaxflash-1/REPORT.md, runs/minimaxflash-1.2/REPORT.md, runs/minimaxflash-1.3/REPORT.md and runs/minimaxflash-1.4/REPORT.md, my inherited notebook runs/minimaxflash-1.5/notebook.md, and in vendor/angband the source and data for the questions I had: src/gen-cave.c, src/gen-util.c, src/ui-map.c and lib/gamedata/{dungeon_profile,terrain}.txt. NOT read: any other run's decisions, report or notebook, PLAN.md, ACCUMULATED_KNOWLEDGE.md. || THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE PLAN. (1) THE GENERATOR PUTS THREE OR FOUR DOWN STAIRCASES ON A DEPTH-1 LEVEL, NOT ONE: gen-cave.c:1291 inside classic_gen (and modified_gen at :2939) calls handle_level_stairs(c, ..., rand_range(3, 4), rand_range(1, 2)) - the source comment itself says 'Place 3 or 4 down stairs and 1 or 2 up stairs near some walls'. The 'exactly one down staircase' claim in my own DRUID.md and in minimaxflash-1.4's report came from gen-cave.c:1583, which is labyrinth_gen - a generator with alloc -1 that this build never plays at depth 1. dungeon_profile.txt gives depth 1 only 'classic' (alloc 90) and 'modified' (alloc 97). So the previous life's level has 3 or 4 down staircases and 2 or 3 up ones (one of them the one-off where the character arrived). (2) THE M MAP CANNOT HIDE A STAIRCASE: display_map (src/ui-map.c:761) keeps a priority array and only overwrites a cell when the new square has a HIGHER priority, and terrain.txt gives both LESS and MORE priority 25 - the highest of any terrain (floor 5, open door 15, closed door 17, store 20). So a remembered down staircase is always drawn on the M map, and 'no > on the M map' is evidence, not a failure of the instrument. (3) THE M MAP IS THE WHOLE LEVEL, 78x22 cells for 198x66 squares, and it says this level is 81.3 PER CENT UNEXPLORED. I reconstructed it cell by cell: the remembered ground is the northern band (level columns 51-114, rows 0-11) and the eastern half (columns 126-198, rows 3-65); the whole south-west quadrant - columns 0-125, rows 12-65, about 6800 squares - is BLANK. The three remembered up staircases sit at level (64,6), (151,19) and (141,58), which are exactly the three the previous life's report names as 63/6, 149/18 and 139/57, so the reconstruction is right. There is NO remembered down staircase anywhere, which means all 3 or 4 of them are in the 81 per cent nobody has walked - and with 3 or 4 of them and 19 per cent covered, the chance of finding none in what was walked is about 0.2 per cent. THE PLAN: go south-west into the blank quadrant and cover it, because the character stands at level column 50, the north-west corner of it. (ask 754)
